BR-34
BRAKE - REAR BRAKE PAD
REPLACEMENT 1. REMOVE REAR WHEEL
2. INSPECT PAD LINING THICKNESS
Check the pad thickness.
Minimum thickness: 1.0 mm (0.039 in,)
N
3. REMOVE CLIP, 2 ANTI-RATTLE SPRINGS AND 2 PAD
GUIDE PINS
--··- (a) Using a screwdriver, remove the clip and 2 anti-rattle
springs.
NOTICE:
• Do not deform the clip and anti-rattle spring. ··• . • The clip and anti-rattle spring can be used again pro•
vided that they have sufficient rebound, no deforma• {1J
N tion, cracks or wear, and have had all rust, di rt and for•
elgn particles cleaned off.
(b) Remove the 2 pad guide pins.
4. REMOVE PADS AND ANTJ.-SQUEAL SHIMS
(a) Remove the 2 pads.
(b) Remove the anti-squeal shim from each pad.
5. CHECK DISC THICKNESS AND RUNOUT
{see page BR-39)
6. INSTALL NEW PADS
NOTICE:
When replacing worn pads, the anti-squeal shims must be
replaced together with the pads.
(a) Apply disc brake grease to inside of anti-squeal shfms
(See page BR-33).
(b) Install the anti-squeal shim on each pad.
(c} Draw out a small amount of brake fluid from the reservoir.
(d) Press in the piston with a hammer handle or equivalent.
HINT:
• Tape the hammer handle before use.
• If the piston is difficult to push in, loosen the bleeder plug
and push in the piston while letting some brake fluid es·
cape.
(e) Install the inner pad with the pad wear indicator plats fac­
ing upward, and install the outer pad.
